[residency_at_reason: preceptor-untitled] Blakemore's residency began at Johns Hopkins in 1922, the year of Halsted's death, and continued at Henry Ford Hospital (Detroit) and Roosevelt Hospital (New York). Vaughan A, Nagendran M, Cohen S. 'Arthur Hendley Blakemore's life and contributions to vascular surgery.' J Vasc Surg. 2014 (PMID 25449007) records that in New York he trained under Dr Richard H. Derby, described only as a notable surgeon; no chair, chief, program-director or associate-program-director title is documented for Derby in that source or in the Roosevelt Hospital surgical leadership record for the period, which names McBurney and subsequently Weir and Bull. The preceptor is therefore identified by name but structurally untitled, which is the preceptor-untitled case and not director-unidentified. No person-to-person direct_training edge is authored: Carter 1952 covers Halsted appointees only and cannot name Blakemore, and the prior edge's own notes conceded he likely trained under post-Halsted leadership. Citation upgraded institutional_archive -> PMID as part of this conversion.

notes: route: 01_halsted_core [V15] TRUE incoming lineage for Blalock, replacing the retired false JHH-as-Halsted edge. Blalock was DENIED the Halsted residency (average record); after a Hopkins urology internship + a non-renewed assistant residency, he completed formative training under Barney Brooks (Vanderbilt's first Professor/Chief of Surgery) from Sept 1925, becoming Vanderbilt's first chief resident. Brooks himself was a Halsted pupil, so this correctly seats Blalock as Halsted's GRAND-pupil (Halsted->Brooks->Blalock), not a direct Halstedian.
